---
title: "What It Costs to Get Home for Thanksgiving"
subtitle: "81.5 million Americans are traveling. Flights are up 17%, gas is up 74 cents from last year, and driving still wins by a mile."
author: "SixtyEight95"
date: "2026-11-24"
categories: [holidays, travel, cost of living]
image: infographic.png
---


::: {.cell}

:::


AAA expects **81.5 million Americans** to travel at least 50 miles for Thanksgiving this year, between
Tuesday, Nov 24 to Monday, Nov 30. That's about the same as last year's record (81.6 million). Getting there costs more than
it did last year, though, whether you drive or fly.

## The short answer

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
For a family of four going 500 miles each way, the round trip is about **$152 in gas** in a car that gets
25 mpg, up from about **$122** last Thanksgiving. Flying the same family costs about **$3,200**, with
holiday roundtrip tickets averaging **$800**, up **17%**. If you're driving, leave in the **morning**.
On Thanksgiving Day itself, the roads are nearly empty.
:::

## How people are getting there


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


Table: Source: AAA Thanksgiving Holiday Travel Forecast, Nov 16, 2026.

|How they're traveling | 2026 travelers|
|:---------------------|--------------:|
|Car                   |   72.9 million|
|Plane (domestic)      |   5.96 million|
|Bus, train, or cruise |    2.6 million|
|Total                 |   81.5 million|


:::
:::


Nearly **9 in 10** holiday travelers drive. AAA expects about 200,000 fewer people on the road than last year, partly because
of high gas prices. Travel by bus, train, and cruise is up about 4%.

## Driving: gas is high, but falling

The national average for regular gas was **$3.81 a gallon** the week of November 16, according to the Energy
Information Administration. That's down from over $4 a few weeks ago, but still **$0.74 more** than
Thanksgiving week last year ($3.06).

AAA notes that the average price on Thanksgiving Day has **never been above $4** and that the record is **$3.58**,
set in 2022. With prices where they are, this year could set a new one.

**What a trip costs in gas** (round trip, 25 mpg car):


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Round trip | Gallons| Cost this year| Cost last Thanksgiving|
|:----------|-------:|--------------:|----------------------:|
|200 miles  |       8|            $30|                    $24|
|500 miles  |      20|            $76|                    $61|
|1000 miles |      40|           $152|                   $122|


:::
:::


## Flying: up 17%

AAA says domestic roundtrip flights booked for the holiday average **$800 per ticket**, **17% more** than
last year. Government price data tells a similar story: airline fares in the Consumer Price Index were up
**22%** in September compared with a year earlier.

For a family of four, that's about **$3,200** in tickets alone, before bags and the drive to the airport.

## When to leave

INRIX, which tracks traffic, says the worst times to drive are **afternoons and early evenings**, and the best are
**mornings**. Big metros like New York, Washington, Los Angeles, and Boston could see more than double their normal congestion.


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


Table: Source: INRIX, via AAA. Times are local.

|Day         |Worst time to drive |Best time to drive |
|:-----------|:-------------------|:------------------|
|Tue, Nov 24 |2–8 PM              |Before 1 PM        |
|Wed, Nov 25 |Noon–7 PM           |Before noon        |
|Thu, Nov 26 |Minimal traffic     |Anytime            |
|Fri, Nov 27 |1–7 PM              |Before noon        |
|Sat, Nov 28 |Noon–9 PM           |Before 11 AM       |
|Sun, Nov 29 |Noon–8 PM           |Before 11 AM       |
|Mon, Nov 30 |2–7 PM              |Before 1 PM        |


:::
:::


## The fine print

- **AAA's traveler numbers** are forecasts of people traveling 50+ miles from home between Nov 24 and Nov 30.
- **The $800 airfare** is AAA's average for domestic roundtrip tickets booked for the holiday. Your fare will depend on route
  and timing.
- **Gas prices** are EIA weekly national averages. AAA's own daily average runs slightly differently, so its Thanksgiving
  record is AAA's number.
- **Our trip example** counts gas only, not tolls, wear and tear, or parking.

Safe travels, and happy Thanksgiving.

---

**How we did this.** Traveler forecasts, airfares, and best and worst travel times are from AAA's Thanksgiving forecast
(with INRIX), released November 16, 2026. Gas prices are EIA weekly retail prices via FRED (series GASREGW). Airfare price
changes are from the BLS Consumer Price Index for airline fares via FRED (CUUR0000SETG01).
